steps.content: For some people, power is a sweet burden that makes them crave the superiority to match. Laws, morals, general equality... all become sources of discontent. Deep down, they hunger to stand above the masses. Trampling on other people has lost its novelty; what they truly desire is to crush rules and reason.

And so, Euphoria became the perfect choice. After all, anyone can buy the company of celebrities and socialites in DisCity, but few have the nerve to entertain themselves with Sinners; ordinary people lack the means, or the rights. Now this is the true privilege.

Once a few of these rotten old leeches were reeled in, it was natural that a clientele eager to gain their favor would follow. Through careful dealings and a constantly grown legend, Euphoria was shaped into the fabled haven among the elites.

That's what Cassian explained, though Sallie doesn't quite understand. Not being a Sinner makes her less popular, which also leaves her free to listen in from the corners. It doesn't take long for her to pick up on something.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Heh, I heard that good-for-nothing son of theirs got dumped by some woman. He's been moping at home since.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: We all told him to get out, have some fun. Play around with girls, sure. But a club dancer? Dude's got no standards.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: If you ask me, with how shaky things are right now, he should forget about the chick and focus on shoring up his connections. His family doesn't have much to their name. Who knows, they'd be back to square one any day.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: They might want connections, but others might not want theirs. A lot goes into marriage alliances: money, power, social circles. Can't afford to ignore any of those.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Haha, well, that's what this place is for! Blow off some steam, have a little fun, and still get some real business done.

Sallie barely dares to breathe, her heart pounding. She glances at Milly, who makes an excited heart sign with her hands. She sneaks a look at Cassian. The bartender gives no outward sign, but offers the slightest of nods. So... they really are talking about Theodore?
She wants to hear more, to learn about his situation. Why did they say he was dumped. What happened?
But love affairs are too common in Eastside to warrant discussion. The conversation has already moved on.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Only he has the luxury of moping about a breakup. We have bigger problems to worry about! A lot of backdoor deals got investigated after the Great Expo. My old man's terrified they'll start coming for everyone who greased Fraser's wheels at the <color=#fb9259>Sillage Society</color>.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Hey, you got any inside info on that?

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Me? I do stocks, how would I know about that stuff? Last time I heard about... Fraser infiltrating DisCity, it was from you guys here.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: Shh... keep it down! You don't talk about that in the open. Walls have ears. Someone might get the dirt on you.

steps.speaker: Guest D
steps.content: Ha, you must be new here. Still learning the ropes, huh? Let me put it this way: this is the only safe place to talk. Euphoria's lips are sealed, and none of us here would ever rat each other out. Nobody wants to hear Mr. E say to them...

steps.speaker: Guest D
steps.content: "You wouldn't want word getting out about your visits here, would you?" Hahahaha! See? We're all in the same boat!

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Exactly. And here's some good news. I heard from <color=#fb9259>Sillage</color> that the Bureau Chief is dead! You know, the one who wouldn't stop yelling about catching traitors? The clown's gone, for real!
The lounge erupts in laughter. Sallie doesn't quite understand what they were saying, but in that moment, she feels an inexplicable chill.

In a corner of the room, as the crowd cheers for one person's death, Milly, whose smile is usually as brilliant as the sun, suddenly turns ice-cold. Her face falls into shadow, her hand clenching her wine glass. A dinner knife lies not far from her reach.
The moment sends chills down Sallie's spine. But the celebrating crowd clearly has no idea of the impending danger.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: You know, that dog from the 9th Agency. Got beaten half to death at the Great Expo, gone missing now. They say there's a new Black Ring—BR-005.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Sillage says the Chief was linked to the Black Ring and the Mania rotted him away. Great job, Fraser. A Black Ring that big? No way he's still kicking after that.
steps.female_content: Sillage says the Chief was linked to the Black Ring and the Mania rotted her away. Great job, Fraser. A Black Ring that big? No way she's still kicking after that.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Well, that's the best news I've heard all day! Serves him right for hounding us! Come, raise your glass, my friends! It's time to celebrate!
steps.female_content: Well, that's the best news I've heard all day! Serves her right for hounding us! Come, raise your glass, my friends! It's time to celebrate!

steps.content: Bang—
The sound that follows isn't the clear clink of a toast, but the explosive crack of shattering glass.
Rather than raising her glass in toast, Milly crushes it in her grip. The blood-red liquid runs through her fingers, dripping slowly to the floor.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: What the hell?! What's your problem?!
The festive atmosphere is shattered. All eyes turn toward the disturbance, the air suddenly tense.
Sallie turns at the sound and stares into a face pale as death. Milly's eyes are vacant but sharp. She's ready to tear apart everything in her sight.
Dropping the shattered glass, she snatches the dinner knife. Her shoulders tense, coiling to lunge into the crowd.
Without time to think, Sallie throws herself forward and wraps her arms tightly around Milly.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: It's nothing. She's just... so excited, she got a little carried away... broke her glass and cut her hand. I'll take her to get it cleaned up.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: Milly, you've had too much to drink... Come on, let's step outside for some air, okay?

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: <size=30>I know you're hurting, but this isn't the time to break down... Please, not here. Don't let them see you like this.</size>
She turns to Milly, speaking in a hushed whisper while reaching out to grip Milly's wrists, shielding the knife in Milly's right hand with her body.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: Please, Milly. For my sake... okay?

They stand locked together for a moment. Finally, with a tremble through her shoulders, Milly's clenched fingers slowly loosen. The knife slips from her grasp and clatters to the floor with a sharp, cold clang.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Just a minor accident. Please, don't let it spoil your evening.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Tsk... Get her out of here! Totally ruined the mood.
Cassian steps out from behind the bar to calm the startled guests, positioning himself between Milly and the crowd.
Meanwhile, under the cover of the other dancers, Sallie helps Milly get away from the scene.
